## 1 · Relational model · DDL
**Relation** = table; **attribute** = column (atomic type = **domain**: INTEGER, REAL, CHAR(n), TEXT); **tuple** = row.
**Schema** = name + attrs (~type, stable). **Instance** = set of tuples (~value, changes). DB schema = set of relation schemas.
```
CREATE TABLE Author(
  authorid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  firstname CHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  lastname CHAR(30),
  email TEXT UNIQUE);
-- composite: PRIMARY KEY(name,category)
INSERT INTO Author
  VALUES(1,'Dan','Brown');
INSERT INTO Author(authorid, lastname)
  VALUES(2,'Verne');
UPDATE Author SET authorid=5
  WHERE authorid=1;
DELETE FROM Author WHERE authorid=1;
DROP TABLE Book;
```
**PRIMARY KEY**: minimal unique id; **exactly one** per table; **no NULLs**. Dup insert → rejected.
**UNIQUE**: also unique id; **many** allowed. NULLs in UNIQUE: prof said **not allowed** (answer that on his exam); standard SQL/SQLite do allow them.
**VIEW** `CREATE VIEW V AS SELECT…` — virtual, not stored; query re-run each use; usable like a table in queries. ❌ can't INSERT/DELETE rows of a view (quiz).
Atomic = can't subdivide (❌ array/list/struct). Table **without PK allowed** → duplicate rows OK. `DEFAULT v` fills omitted INSERT cols (else NULL). `DELETE FROM T` (no WHERE) empties, table stays; `DROP TABLE T` removes schema+data. Empty table = valid instance.
View vs WITH: WITH lives for **one query**; view persists. View = stored SQL text, **inlined** into each query (never materialized); `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT` materializes.

## 2 · Foreign keys
```
FOREIGN KEY (authorid)
  REFERENCES Author(authorid)
  ON DELETE CASCADE
  ON UPDATE SET NULL
```
Referenced attrs **must be PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE**. Every non-NULL `Book.authorid` must exist in `Author`.
Violations (R=Book references S=Author): ① insert/update in **R** with value not in S ② delete/update in **S** leaves R tuples **dangling**.

| policy | delete/update of S row |
|---|---|
| **reject** (default) | refused |
| CASCADE | S row deleted/updated; del → referencing R rows deleted; upd → new key copied into R |
| SET NULL | S row deleted/updated; referencing R values → NULL (R rows stay) |

Choose independently for UPDATE and DELETE: 3×3 = **9** combos (prof said 6 in class). Policies only affect changes to **S**; bad insert into **R** always rejected. SQLite: `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`.

> [!ok] Quiz (ON DELETE CASCADE): del Book → Author deleted? **F** · del Author → Book always deleted? **F** (only if referenced) · add Author → Book unchanged **T** · add Book never rejected? **F**
Referencing col (Book.authorid) need **not** be unique. Composite: `FOREIGN KEY(a,b) REFERENCES S(x,y)`. Effects flow **opposite** the reference arrow; CASCADE can chain. Lecture: update Book.authorid→100 (not in Author) ❌; delete referenced Author ❌ (dangling).

## 3 · Single-table SELECT
```
SELECT [DISTINCT] a, expr AS alias
FROM R          -- SELECT * = all attrs
WHERE cond      -- selection (rows)
ORDER BY a DESC, b    -- ASC default
LIMIT n;
```
Semantics: tuple var ranges over R → keep if WHERE **TRUE** → compute SELECT.
**Bag semantics** by default (dups kept); `DISTINCT` → set. DISTINCT on a key ⇒ same #rows (quiz).
WHERE: `=` `<>` `<` `>` `<=` `>=`, `+ - * /`, AND OR NOT, `||` concat, LIKE, `IS [NOT] NULL`, BETWEEN, `IN (…)`.
`LIKE`: `%` = any sequence (incl. empty), `_` = exactly one char. `LIKE 'monarchy'` = exact match only!
Strings in **'single quotes'**. `Population/1000000` = **integer division**; use `/1000000.0`.
ORDER BY ties broken by next key; can use alias. ORDER BY+LIMIT 1 ≠ `= (SELECT MAX…)` when **ties** (LIMIT drops them).
```
CASE WHEN c1 THEN v1
     WHEN c2 THEN v2
     ELSE v END
```
First true WHEN wins; no ELSE → NULL. Usable in SELECT, inside aggregates, with EXISTS.
`ROUND(x,2)` · `substr(s,i,len)` (1-indexed) · `group_concat(v)`
`SELECT DISTINCT a` → **fewer or same** rows; without DISTINCT → same #rows. DISTINCT **costs more** (sort/hash). No ORDER BY ⇒ row order **not guaranteed**. `LIMIT` takes a constant, after ORDER BY. Use the original column name in WHERE, not the SELECT alias. Parenthesize mixed AND/OR. WHERE is per row → comparing 2 rows needs self-join.

## 4 · Multi-table queries (joins)
```
SELECT C.Name
FROM Country C, CountryLanguage L1,
     CountryLanguage L2
WHERE C.Code = L1.CountryCode
  AND C.Code = L2.CountryCode
  AND L1.Language = 'Greek'
  AND L2.Language = 'English';
```
Qualify ambiguous attrs `R.a`; aliases **required** for self-join (2 copies). Unqualified shared names = bad style.
**Semantics:** ① cross product of FROM ② filter WHERE ③ project SELECT ④ DISTINCT dedup. = nested loops `for t1∈R1 … for tn∈Rn: if cond: add`. DBMS evaluates smarter (declarative).

```
SELECT R.D FROM R, S
WHERE R.A=S.B AND S.C='e'
```
| R(A,D) | S(B,C) | steps |
|---|---|---|
| 1a 2b 2c | 1d 2e | × 6 rows → σ (2b2e),(2c2e) → π **b, c** |

$|R\times S|=|R|\cdot|S|$ rows. Join with no WHERE = cross product. `A JOIN B ON c` ≡ `FROM A,B WHERE c`.

> [!warn] Greek **and** English: one copy `L.Language='Greek' AND L.Language='English'` → **empty** (one cell can't be both); `OR` → either. ✓ two copies L1, L2 (3 langs → L3).

Key–FK joins ≈ 90%. `ON` may be any condition; JOINs chain.

## 5 · Aggregation · GROUP BY · HAVING
`SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX`; `COUNT(*)` = #rows; `COUNT(DISTINCT a)` dedups first. Aggregates **ignore NULLs** (`COUNT(a)` skips NULL a; `COUNT(*)` doesn't).
```
SELECT [DISTINCT] S
FROM R, S, …   WHERE C1
GROUP BY attrs HAVING C2
ORDER BY …     LIMIT n;
```
**Eval order:** FROM-WHERE → GROUP → HAVING (keep groups) → SELECT aggs → ORDER BY → LIMIT.

> [!warn] **Rule:** with GROUP BY/aggs, each SELECT item is **aggregated or in GROUP BY**. HAVING may use aggregates + GROUP BY attrs only. WHERE filters **rows** (no aggs); HAVING filters **groups**.

| R(A,B,C) | SELECT A, SUM(B\*C) GROUP BY A |
|---|---|
| a2 0 · a5 1 · b7 1 · b6 0 · c4 1 | a **5** · b **7** · c **4**; HAVING >5 → only b |

> [!ok] Quiz Book(bookid,title,authorid), GROUP BY authorid. Valid: SELECT `COUNT(bookid)` ✓ · `COUNT(bookid), authorid` ✓ · HAVING `COUNT(bookid)>1` ✓. Invalid: SELECT `title` ❌ · HAVING `bookid=1` ❌ · GROUP BY brand HAVING `price>100` ❌

Group by a key ⇒ every group has 1 row. No GROUP BY + agg ⇒ one output row (whole table = 1 group).
Countries with ≥10 cities: GROUP BY `C.Name` HAVING `COUNT(T.ID)>9`. HAVING with join usually **faster** than correlated COUNT subquery.
**HAVING requires GROUP BY.** HAVING may use SELECT alias (`… AS N … HAVING N>2`) and a different agg than SELECT. GROUP BY acts like DISTINCT (1 row/group). Agg without GROUP BY → 1×1 table. **All NULLs form ONE group** (GROUP BY and DISTINCT treat NULLs as equal, despite NULL=NULL → U). Ill-formed GROUP BY (`SELECT Continent … GROUP BY Code`) **runs in SQLite** (arbitrary value) but is ❌ on exam.

## 6 · Nested queries
Subquery = value or table (SQL is **compositional**: every result is a multiset). Allowed in **FROM** (needs `AS` alias), **WHERE**, or factored out with `WITH`:
```
WITH C AS (SELECT Name, Continent
           FROM Country
           WHERE Population > 50000000),
     D AS (…)   -- several, comma-sep.
SELECT C.Name FROM C
WHERE C.Continent = 'Europe';
```
**Scalar** (above-average European country):
```
WHERE C.Continent = 'Europe'
  AND C.Population >
   (SELECT AVG(Population) FROM Country
    WHERE Continent = 'Europe')
```
**Argmax with name** (keeps ties): `Population =` `(SELECT MAX(Population) …)`. **Per group** (top earner per dept) = correlated:
```
SELECT E.name, E.salary FROM Emp E
WHERE E.salary = (SELECT MAX(E2.salary)
   FROM Emp E2 WHERE E2.dept = E.dept)
```

| op | true when |
|---|---|
| x IN (Q) · NOT IN | x is / isn't in Q |
| EXISTS (Q) · NOT EXISTS | Q non-empty / empty |
| x op ANY (Q) | op holds for **some** row |
| x op ALL (Q) | op for **every** row (T if Q empty) |

op before ANY/ALL must be a comparison. SQLite has no ANY/ALL.
**Correlated** = inner query uses an **outer** variable → re-run per outer row. Merely nested ≠ correlated (quiz — **not** correlated):
```
WHERE stid NOT IN (SELECT s.stid
  FROM Student s, Enrolled e
  WHERE s.stid = e.stid
    AND e.numcredits > 3)
```
**∃ "some city > 5M"** — all equivalent:
```
AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM City T
    WHERE T.Population > 5000000
    AND T.CountryCode = C.Code)
AND C.Code IN (SELECT CountryCode
    FROM City WHERE Population>5000000)
AND 5000000 <= ANY (SELECT T.Population
    FROM City T
    WHERE T.CountryCode = C.Code)
-- unnested: join + DISTINCT
SELECT DISTINCT C.Name
FROM Country C, City T
WHERE C.Continent = 'Europe'
  AND T.CountryCode = C.Code
  AND T.Population > 5000000
```
**∀ "all cities < 1M"** = ¬∃ violator:
```
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM City T
    WHERE T.Population > 1000000
    AND T.CountryCode = C.Code)
AND 1000000 > ALL (SELECT T.Population
    FROM City T
    WHERE T.CountryCode = C.Code)
-- or: Europe countries EXCEPT
--   Europe countries ⋈ City > 1M
```
Unnest ∃/IN → join **+ DISTINCT** (join duplicates outer rows). ∀/NOT EXISTS can't be a plain join → EXCEPT.

> [!ok] Quiz 4: WHERE `color='green'` GROUP BY brand HAVING `COUNT(*)<3` ≡ only the version with **DISTINCT** brand + outer `color='green'` + correlated COUNT of q with `q.brand=p.brand` AND `q.color='green'` `< 3`. No DISTINCT → dups ❌. No outer green filter → brands with 0 green ❌.
`x op (Q)` needs Q = **1 row × 1 col** (else IN/ANY/ALL/EXISTS). Correlated only in **WHERE** (not FROM/WITH); **slower** (runs per outer row). WITH tables may reference earlier ones.
∀ also via grouping: GROUP BY `C.Code` HAVING `MAX(T.Population)<1000000`. ⚠ NOT EXISTS keeps outer rows with **no** inner rows (vacuously true); GROUP BY form drops them. NULL value escapes a violator test (`sal<=50000` is U).

> [!info] Exam: nested **and** unnested answers both accepted.

## 7 · Set operators
`(Q1) UNION | INTERSECT | EXCEPT (Q2)` — **set** semantics, dups removed. Add `ALL` → bag semantics. Same #cols/types. SQLite: only UNION ALL; groups set ops **left-to-right**.
R = {1,1,1,2,3}, S = {1,1,2,2,4,5}:

| op | result | copies |
|---|---|---|
| UNION | 1 2 3 4 5 | |
| INTERSECT | 1 2 | |
| R EXCEPT S | 3 | |
| S EXCEPT R | 4 5 | |
| UNION ALL | 1×5 2×3 3 4 5 | $m+n$ |
| INTERSECT ALL | 1 1 2 | $\min(m,n)$ |
| EXCEPT ALL | 1 3 | $\max(m-n,0)$ |

No set op needed:
```
-- R INTERSECT S
SELECT DISTINCT R.A FROM R, S
WHERE R.A = S.A
-- R ∩ (S ∪ T)  ⚠ wrong if S or T empty
SELECT DISTINCT R.A FROM R, S, T
WHERE R.A=S.A OR R.A=T.A
```
Greek **and** English speakers: self-join L1,L2 **or** INTERSECT of two queries.
UNION, INTERSECT symmetric; **EXCEPT not** (R−S ≠ S−R). Schemas must match.

## 8 · NULLs · 3-valued logic
NULL = missing (unknown value) or inapplicable (spouse of unmarried). Not allowed in PK.
Arithmetic/concat with NULL → **NULL** (`(10*x)+5`, `NULL/0`, `'a'||NULL`). Any comparison with NULL (even `NULL=NULL`) → **UNKNOWN**.
TRUE=1, UNKNOWN=½, FALSE=0: **AND = min, OR = max, NOT = 1−v**. WHERE/HAVING keep row only if **TRUE**.

| | T | U | F |
|---|---|---|---|
| U AND · | U | U | F |
| U OR · | T | U | U |

`x>1990 OR x<=1990` **skips NULL rows** → add `OR x IS NULL`. Test only with `IS NULL / IS NOT NULL`.
`x NOT IN (…NULL…)` is never TRUE ⚠.

> [!ok] Quiz: rows (1,NULL,red),(2,200,NULL),(3,NULL,NULL); `WHERE price>100 OR color<>'green'` → **1, 2** (row 3: U OR U = U). `WHERE price<>100` never returns NULL-price rows ✓ True.

> [!ok] Ex: A=1,B=NULL,C=NULL: `A>0 AND (B<5 OR NOT C=3)` = min(1, max(½,½)) = ½ → not returned.
NULL ≠ `''`: `'a'||''`='a', `'a'||NULL`=NULL. `IS NULL` is the only comparison that is never UNKNOWN. A row with NULLs can still pass (T AND (U OR T) = T). Exception: GROUP BY / DISTINCT put all NULLs in **one** group. ORDER BY: SQLite puts NULLs first in ASC.

## 9 · Inner / outer joins
`R [INNER] JOIN S ON R.B=S.B` ≡ comma join + WHERE; `SELECT *` keeps **both** R.B and S.B columns. **LEFT OUTER**: keep every R row, pad S attrs with NULL · **RIGHT**: every S row · **FULL**: both.
R(A,B) = a2 a5 b5 c6 · S(B,C) = 2·100 3·200 5·300 7·400; SELECT R.A, R.B, S.C … ON R.B=S.B:

| join | rows |
|---|---|
| INNER | a2 100 · a5 300 · b5 300 |
| LEFT | inner + **c 6 NULL** |
| RIGHT | inner + **NULL 3 200 · NULL 7 400** |
| FULL | inner + all three extras |

Max city per country **incl. countries with no city**:
```
SELECT C.Name, MAX(T.Population)
FROM Country C
  LEFT OUTER JOIN City T
  ON C.Code = T.CountryCode
GROUP BY C.Name;  -- no city: MAX=NULL
```
Counting after outer join: `COUNT(T.ID)` → 0, `COUNT(*)` → 1 ⚠.

## 10 · HW1 / activity patterns
**Matrices** A(i,j,val), B(i,j,val):
```
-- A + B
SELECT A.i, A.j, A.val + B.val
FROM A, B WHERE A.i=B.i AND A.j=B.j;
-- A · B (row i of A · col j of B)
SELECT A.i, B.j, SUM(A.val * B.val)
FROM A, B WHERE A.j = B.i
GROUP BY A.i, B.j;
-- dot(1st col of A, 2nd col of B)
-- HW1 indexes are 0-based!
SELECT SUM(A.val*B.val) FROM A, B
WHERE A.i=B.i AND A.j=0 AND B.j=1;
-- yes/no row: ∀ agree ⇔ ¬∃ differ
SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT * FROM A X, A Y
  WHERE X.i = Y.j AND X.j = Y.i
    AND X.val <> Y.val)
 THEN 'TRUE' ELSE 'FALSE'
 END AS IsSymmetric;
```
Commutative AB=BA: same pattern, compare two product subqueries (WITH) on (i,j).
**Pivot** (rows → columns) with CASE inside AVG (no ELSE → NULL, ignored):
```
SELECT Type,
 ROUND(AVG(CASE
   WHEN substr(WeekDate,6,2)
        IN ('12','01','02')
   THEN WeeklySales END), 2) AS Winter,
 …
FROM Sales S, Stores T
WHERE S.Store = T.Store
GROUP BY Type;
```
**Graphs** Edge(source, target, d):
```
-- out-degree
SELECT source, COUNT(target)
FROM Edge GROUP BY source;
-- 2-hop paths + distance
SELECT e1.source, e2.target,
       e1.d + e2.d
FROM Edge e1, Edge e2
WHERE e1.target = e2.source;
```
Edge has **no PK** (multigraph) → joins are self-joins; path of length k = k copies chained `ei.target=ej.source`. WITH RECURSIVE needs a stop condition. Streets stored twice (A→B and B→A): drop mirror pairs with `A<B`; ≤3 hops = UNION of 1-, 2-, 3-hop joins; triangle = 3-way self-join closing back, nodes pairwise `<>`.
**Window fn:** `row_number() OVER (ORDER BY A)`. Consecutive runs: GROUP BY `A - row_number()`, then MIN, MAX, COUNT(*). Median (odd n): row where `2*rn = n+1`.
**Recursion:**
```
WITH RECURSIVE cnt(x) AS (
  VALUES(1) UNION ALL
  SELECT x+1 FROM cnt WHERE x < 4)
SELECT x FROM cnt;     -- 1 2 3 4
```

## 11 · E/R model (Chen 1976)
Build app: requirements → **ER diagram** → relational schema → **normalize** → implement.
**Entity** = distinguishable object; **entity set** = □ rectangle; **attribute** = ◯ oval (key **underlined**); **relationship** = ◇ diamond, mathematically $R\subseteq A\times B$ (a **set**: each (a,b) pair at most once).
#### Multiplicity
Arrow points to the **"one"** side = "at most one":

| | drawing | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| many-many | A — ◇ — B | no arrows |
| many-one | A — ◇ → B | each A ↦ ≤1 B (Product makes→ Company) |
| one-one | A ← ◇ → B | both directions ≤1 |
| exactly one | A — ◇ —) B | rounded arrow: **referential integrity** (=1, must exist) |

#### Multi-way · roles · ISA · weak
**Multi-way:** arrow to E ⇒ the **other** entities together determine ≤1 E. Product—purchase→Store, Person: (person,product) → ≤1 store. Two arrows: also (store,person) → ≤1 product. "Person buys from ≤1 store" **not expressible** (approx. only).
**Roles:** same entity set twice → label edges (buyer, salesperson), draw set once. **Relationship attributes** (date on purchase) allowed.
**Multi-way → binary:** make relationship an entity set (Purchase) with **many-one** arrows to each participant (productOf→, storeOf→, buyerOf→).
**ISA** △ subclass: specialized, fewer entities, more attrs; **inherits** attrs (+ key).
**Weak entity set** (double □, supporting rel. double ◇, rounded arrow to owner): key = own partial key (number) + owner key (University.name).
#### Fine print (lectures)
**Arrows** (each arrow = separate constraint, ANDed); notation = slides (◇→ at "one" side), not cow book. Individual entities not drawn. Roles: salesperson edge may carry arrow (≤1 per purchase), buyer edge none.
3 binary rels ≠ 1 ternary (lose which product at which store). Ternary → Purchase entity is only an approximation (arrows = ≤1); keeping ternary is fine.
**Keys in ER:** every entity set **exactly one** key (diagram wrong without); several underlined attrs = **one composite** key; no natural key → add ID; ≥1 attribute. Attributes single-valued, carry no arrows → multi-valued (phones) = new entity set + relationship.
**ISA** must be a **tree** (no 2 superclasses); triangle top = superclass.
**Weak:** supporting rel. must be **binary + exactly one** (rounded): 0 or 2 owners ⇒ no unique key.
Over-constrained: arrow Buys→Product = person buys ≤1 product ❌.

#### Constraints (find as many as possible)
**Key** (ssn identifies person; every entity set needs one; ≥1 attr; several possible, 1 primary — no formal multi-key notation) · **single-value** (≤1 father; attribute or many-one) · **referential integrity** (works-for company must exist) · **domain** (0≤age≤150) · **other** (≤80 enrolled).
Why: semantics, prevent bad data, refer to entities, efficient storage/lookup.
#### Design principles
① **Faithful** (❌ purchase→Product arrow = person buys ≤1 product, should be many-many; ❌ Country—president—Person no arrows, should be one-one) ② **Avoid redundancy** (❌ personName/personAddress as purchase attrs → make Person entity; ❌ Beer.manufacturer attr *and* manfBy→Manufacturer(name, address) → drop attr) → wasted space, inconsistency ③ **Keep it simple** (❌ Date entity on purchase → `date` attribute) ④ **Attributes over entity sets**: entity set only if it has a non-key attr **or** is the "many" side of many-one/many-many (❌ Beer→Manufacturer(name) only → `manf` attr of Beer; with address or many-many → keep entity) ⑤ **Don't overuse weak entities** — create IDs (SSN, ISBN).

## 12 · ER → relational
| ER | relation |
|---|---|
| entity set E | E(attrs), PK = E's key |
| relationship R (many-many) | R(keys of all participants + R's attrs); PK = union of keys; FKs to each |
| many-one A→B | **no table**: add B's key (+R attrs) to A |
| one-one | fold into either side |
| weak entity W | W(own attrs + owner key); supporting rel. → **no table** |
| ISA | ① table per class, **all** attrs ② subclass = key + own attrs ③ one table, NULLs for N/A |

```
Person(ssn, name, address)
Product(name, category, price)
Buys(prodname, prodcategory, ssn, date)
  PRIMARY KEY(prodname, prodcategory,
              ssn),
  FOREIGN KEY(ssn) REFERENCES Person,
  FOREIGN KEY(prodname, prodcategory)
    REFERENCES Product(name, category)
-- many-one "makes" folded in:
Product(name, category, price,
        company_name)
-- weak entity:
Team(number, affiliatedUniversity,
     sport)
```
❌ putting `ssn` into Product for many-many Buys (1 buyer per product, redundancy).
ISA (slides: Product key = name): ① SoftwareProduct(name, category, price, version) — redundant ② **keep** Product(name, category, price) + SoftwareProduct(name, version), EducationalProduct(name, age_group); subclass key = FK to Product — no redundancy, join for inherited attrs ③ Product(name, category, price, version, age_group) — NULLs waste space, can't forbid both, NULL ambiguous.
Many-one fold also moves R's attrs into the many side.

> [!ok] Handout: Doctor(id, name, age) — Appts(date, time) — Patient(SSN, name, insurance), no arrows → Doctor, Patient, **Appts(id, SSN, date, time)** PK(id, SSN), FKs. Gotcha: relationship = set ⇒ ≤1 appt per pair; repeats → add date/time to key or Appointment entity. **Quiz 8:** 3 tables · Doctor 3 attrs · Appts 4 attrs · 2 FKs.

## 13 · Functional dependencies
$A_1..A_n\to B_1..B_m$: any 2 tuples agreeing on all $A$'s agree on all $B$'s. Generalizes keys. **Domain knowledge** — instance can only **refute** (2 rows same A, diff B) or "seem valid", never prove.
**Split right OK:** $AB\to CD\iff AB\to C,\ AB\to D$. **Never split left:** $AB\to C\not\Rightarrow A\to C$.
#### Armstrong & closure
**Trivial:** $X\to A$ with $A\in X$ (always holds).
**Armstrong** (sound + complete for $F^+$): **Reflexivity** $Y\subseteq X\Rightarrow X\to Y$ · **Augmentation** $X\to Y\Rightarrow XZ\to YZ$ · **Transitivity** $X\to Y, Y\to Z\Rightarrow X\to Z$. (Derived, not axioms: union, decomposition/split, pseudo-trans.)
> Proof $name\to color$, $color\,category\to price$ ⊢ $name\,category\to price$: aug. by category → $name\,cat\to color\,cat$; trans. → $price$. ⊢ $name\,cat\to color$: refl. $name\,cat\to name$ + trans.

**$F^+$** = all FDs implied by F. **$X^+$** = all attrs B with $X\to B$.
**Closure algorithm:** X ← attrs; repeat until no change: if $B_1..B_m\to C$ and all $B_i\in X$, add C.
Ex R(ABCDEF): $AB\to C, AD\to E, B\to D, AF\to B$. $\{A,B\}^+$: AB →C →D (B→D) →E (AD→E) = **ABCDE**. $\{A,F\}^+$ = AF→B→C→D→E = **all** ⇒ AF superkey.
Uses: $X\to Y$ holds ⇔ $Y\subseteq X^+$. $F^+$: for each X, for each $Y\subseteq X^+$, output $X\to Y$.
#### Lecture examples
Reading FDs (studentID, semester, course, section, instructor): course, section → instructor ✓; course → instructor ✗ (2 sections); instructor, course → section = instructor teaches ≤1 section of a course; instructor → course = ≤1 course. Never flip sides.
Lecture Product(name, category, color, department, price): $name\to color$, $category\to department$, $color\,category\to price$ ⇒ $name^+$={name,color} (name→department ✗), {name,category}⁺ = all = only key. Instance: Gizmo in Toys and Office ⇒ name→department refuted; name,category→department "don't know".
Computing $F^+$ over all subsets = exponential; use closures.

## 14 · Keys & superkeys
**Superkey**: $X^+$ = all attrs. **Key (candidate)**: minimal superkey — no proper subset is a superkey (check only one-smaller subsets). PK chosen among candidate keys (not just any superkey). Many keys possible: R(ABC), $AB\to C$, $AC\to B$ ⇒ keys AB, AC.
**Fast key search:** attrs never on any RHS ∈ **every** key; attrs only on RHS ∈ **no** key; start from the must-haves, take closure, add attrs as needed.

> [!ok] Quiz 9 R(ABCDEF), $A\to D, A\to E, D\to C, D\to F$: B never on RHS ⇒ in every key. $\{A,B\}^+$=all. Superkeys: **AB, ABC** (not A, not BDE). Key: **AB**. $A\to EF$ implied ✓ ($A^+$=ADECF).
Product(name,category,price,color), $name\to color$, $color\,category\to price$: only key **{name, category}**; superkeys = its supersets.

> [!info] Exam asks "is X a key / superkey?", not "list all keys". Quiz 9: $B^+=B$ ⇒ AB minimal; BDE not superkey (A on no RHS).

## 15 · Decomposition
Bad schema (SSN,name,age,phone; key SSN+phone): redundancy + **update / insert / delete anomalies**. Fix: split R into $R_1,R_2$ with attrs union = R; instance $R_i=\pi_{R_i}(R)$.
#### Lossless join (chase)
**Desiderata:** ① min redundancy ② **lossless-join** ③ **dependency preserving** ④ query performance.
**Lossless-join:** $R_1\bowtie R_2 = R$ (natural join) for every instance satisfying F. (Join never loses rows — lossy = **extra** spurious rows.) ❌ R(name,age,phone)→(name,age),(age,phone).
**Chase test:** one row per $R_i$: attr in $R_i$ → plain (a), else subscripted with the row number ($b_1$ in row 1). Repeat: for violated FD, equalize RHS (plain wins; else same subscript). Lossless ⇔ some row all plain.

| R(ABCDE): $A\to BC$, $D\to E$ | A | B | C | D | E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1(A,D) | a | b₁→**b** | c₁→**c** | d | e₁→**e** |
| R2(A,B,C) | a | b | c | d₂ | e₂ |
| R3(D,E) | a₃ | b₃ | c₃ | d | e |

$D\to E$ fixes row1 E; $A\to BC$ fixes row1 B,C ⇒ row1 plain ⇒ **lossless** ✓.
**2-way shortcut:** $\{R_1,R_2\}$ lossless ⇔ $(R_1\cap R_2)\to R_1$ or $\to R_2$ (common attrs superkey of one side). No common attrs ⇒ lossy (cross product).
#### Dependency preservation
**Dependency preserving:** enforce $F_i$ on each $R_i$ ⇒ F enforced. $F_i$ = **nontrivial FDs of $F^+$** using only $R_i$ attrs (not just F's). R(ABC), $A\to B, B\to C$: R1(A,C) gets $A\to C$. Check: each FD in F follows from $\cup F_i$ (closure using only $F_i$).
❌ R(ABC), $A\to B$, $BC\to A$ → (A,B),(A,C): $BC\to A$ lost; rejoin (a1 b c),(a2 b c) violates it.
**Stop** the chase as soon as **one** row is all plain. R(ABCD), $A\to BC$: (ABC, AD) lossless; (ABC, D) lossy.

> [!warn] Lossless-join is **never optional**; losing an FD is acceptable (just a constraint, not data).

## 16 · BCNF
> **R in BCNF ⇔ every nontrivial $X\to B$ has X a superkey.** Equiv.: every X has $X^+=X$ **or** $X^+$ = all attrs.

Normal forms: 1NF (atomic) ⊃ 2NF ⊃ 3NF ⊃ **BCNF** ⊃ 4NF (more restrictive →). **Any 2-attr relation is BCNF.**
**Check:** for each FD (and implied ones on sub-relations!) compute $X^+$; $X\subsetneq X^+\neq$ all ⇒ violation.
**Decompose:** pick violating $X\to Y$ **exactly as given** (prof's rule; don't expand to $X^+$): $R_1 = X\cup Y$, $R_2 = X\cup(R\setminus Y)$. Project FDs (via closure: e.g. R(ABCD), $A\to B$, $B\to C$, split AB + ACD ⇒ ACD inherits $A\to C$ from $A^+$), recurse until all BCNF. Choice of FD changes result (and dep.-preservation).
Properties: removes redundancy · **always lossless** ($X=R_1\cap R_2$ is key of $R_1$) · **not always dep.-preserving** (may be impossible: R(ABC), $A\to B$, $BC\to A$ → (AB),(AC)). Result not unique — any order/split of RHS valid (Piazza).

> [!ok] Books(author, gender, booktitle, genre, price): $author\to gender$, $booktitle\to genre\,price$. Key {author, booktitle} ⇒ not BCNF. Split on author → **Author(author, gender)** + Books2(author, booktitle, genre, price); split on booktitle → **BookInfo(booktitle, genre, price)** + **BookAuthor(author, booktitle)**.

> [!ok] Person(SSN,name,age,phone), $SSN\to name\,age$ → (SSN,name,age) + (SSN,phone).

> [!ok] Person(SSN,name,age,canDrink), $SSN\to name\,age$, $age\to canDrink$ → (SSN,name,age)+(age,canDrink): lossless + preserving.

Normalization not always good: attrs always used together (join cost), data warehouses (rarely updated).
Repeated key column across tables ≠ redundancy (bounded); author's gender repeated per book = redundancy.

> [!ok] Extra quiz R(RID, PID, FName, LName, AgentID, AgentName, RDate): $PID\to FName\,LName$, $AgentID\to AgentName$, $RID\to PID\,AgentID\,RDate$; key RID. ✓ Passenger(PID, FName, LName) + Agent(AgentID, AgentName) + Reservation(RID, PID, AgentID, RDate). ❌ AgentName left in Reservation (AgentID→AgentName violates). ❌ Reservation without PID/AgentID (LHS must stay; lossy). Superkeys: **rid**, **rid+rdate** (rid on no RHS ⇒ every superkey has it). Implied: rid → p_fname, agent_name ✓ · pid, agent_id → agent_name ✓ · agent_id, rdate → rid ✗ · pid → p_fname, rdate ✗.

## 17 · Worked: Quiz 10
R(ABCDE): $A\to BC$, $B\to C$, $C\to A$, $D\to E$, $E\to D$. A,B,C mutually determine (cycle); D⇔E.
$A^+ = ABC$ ≠ all ⇒ **not BCNF**. Keys: one of {A,B,C} × one of {D,E} → AD, AE, BD, BE, CD, CE.
**Dep. preserving — all ✓:** ABCD,DE (all FDs local) · AB,BCDE ($A\to B, B\to A$ in AB; $B\to C, C\to B, D\leftrightarrow E$ in BCDE ⇒ $C\to B\to A$) · ABC,CD,DE (CD has none needed).
**Lossless:** ABC,DE ✗ (no shared attr) · ABC,CDE ✓ ($C^+\supseteq ABC$) · ABCD,CDE ✓ ($CD$ = key).
**BCNF of R** (class): $D\to E$ → DE + ABCD; $B\to C$ → BC + ABD; $A\to B$ → AB + AD ⇒ **{DE, BC, AB, AD}** (via $B\to A$: AB, BD). Using $A\to BC$ on ABCD → ABC + AD ⇒ **{DE, ABC, AD}**: lossless **and** preserving (A, B, C each key of ABC).

## ⚠ Design traps
- arrow points **at** the "one" side; rounded = exactly one
- ER relationship = **set** of pairs: same (person, product) can't be bought twice → use entity set Purchase
- left side of FD can't be split; right side can
- key = **minimal**; superkey ⊇ key; PK ∈ candidate keys
- project FDs from $F^+$, not F, when checking sub-relations
- BCNF ⇒ lossless always; dependency preservation **not** guaranteed
- any 2-attribute relation is in BCNF
- lossy join = **more** tuples, not fewer
- instance can disprove an FD, never prove one

## ★ Exam & intro facts
Format: MC · T/F · fill-in · short SQL ("not 50 lines"); quizzes come from past exams. 75 min, 23%, not cumulative.
**DB** = organized collection of structured data; **DBMS** = program to manage large DB efficiently + persist it (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB). Why not files: fast lookup, concurrent writes, crash recovery, valid values. DBMS: automates ops, fast retrieval, scales, safe concurrency, crash protection.
**Data model** = concepts for describing data: relational (Codd 1969), key/value, graph, document/JSON, array/tensor, E/R. SQL = declarative (what, not how); standards SQL-92/1999/2011.

## ⚠ SQL traps
- `SELECT` non-grouped attr ❌ · agg in WHERE ❌ (use HAVING) · HAVING on raw attr ❌
- joins multiply rows → `DISTINCT` / `COUNT(DISTINCT …)`
- `NOT IN` + NULL in subquery → empty; comparisons to NULL → UNKNOWN
- `LIMIT 1` loses ties; integer division; `'single'` quotes
- DISTINCT applies to whole row, not one column
- UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT dedup; `ALL` keeps bags
- correlated = references outer var, not just "is nested"

## ✎ Writing a query
① **FROM** tables, alias each; one copy per role (self-join) ② **WHERE** join conds (n tables → n−1) + row filters ③ "per X" → **GROUP BY** X; group conds → **HAVING** ④ **SELECT** only grouped attrs/aggs; **DISTINCT** if joins can dup ⑤ ∀ → NOT EXISTS; argmax → `= (SELECT MAX…)` ⑥ ORDER BY / LIMIT last. Sanity: run on a tiny instance incl. NULLs, ties, empty groups.
